title: Time-resolved synchronization analysis of stacked intrinsic Josephson junctions of a cuprate superconductor with frequency-modulated terahertz radiation spectra
authors: Masashi Miyamoto, Keisuke Mizoguchi, Ryota Kobayashi, Nozomi Yagyu, Manabu Tsujimoto, Itsuhiro Kakeya
abstract: Terahertz radiation from $\text{Bi}_2\text{Sr}_2\text{CaCu}_2\text{O}_{8+δ}$ intrinsic Josephson junctions (IJJs) provides an ideal platform to study the synchronization of a macroscopic quantum system. Here, we present a spectral analysis of a frequency-modulated Josephson plasma emitter coupled with patch antennas. In the unmodulated intensity distribution as a function of radiation frequency $I_{\mathrm{UM}}(ω)$, we observe a double Gaussian peak structure. Crucially, double-peak spectra obtained at a constant bias voltage imply either a rapid temporal distribution of resonances or their simultaneous excitation, driven by the mutual electromagnetic coupling between the IJJ mesa and the antennas. At low modulation frequencies $f_m$, the spectra are well reproduced by the products of $I_{\mathrm{UM}}(ω)$ and frequency combs, yielding a synchronized relaxation time $τ_s \simeq 0.28\text{ ns}$. Incorporating $τ_s$ quantitatively reproduces a drastic spectral transformation observed around $f_m \sim 1\text{ GHz}$, unveiling the sub-nanosecond non-equilibrium dynamics of coupled Josephson plasma.
summary: The study investigates the ultrafast dynamics of Josephson plasma oscillations in cuprate superconductors by analyzing their response to frequency-modulated terahertz radiation. By fitting spectral sidebands with models incorporating a finite synchronization time ($	au_s$), the authors quantify the non-equilibrium plasmon lifetime, providing deep insight into the coupled electrodynamics of these superconducting junctions.
main_problem: The study aims to perform a time-resolved synchronization analysis of stacked intrinsic Josephson junctions (IJJs) in a cuprate superconductor when subjected to frequency-modulated terahertz radiation spectra.
main_result: The analysis successfully estimates a synchronized relaxation time ($	au_s \simeq 0.28	ext{ ns}$) by analyzing spectral transformations, revealing sub-nanosecond non-equilibrium dynamics of the coupled Josephson plasma.
method: The researchers used frequency-modulated terahertz spectroscopy on $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Sr}_2	ext{CaCu}_2	ext{O}_{8+δ}$ IJJs, comparing measured sideband spectra to theoretical models incorporating a finite relaxation time ($	au_s$).
model_or_system: The physical system is a Josephson Plasma Emitter (JPE) formed by stacked intrinsic Josephson junctions in the cuprate superconductor $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Sr}_2	ext{CaCu}_2	ext{O}_{8+δ}$, coupled with external patch antennas. The dynamics are governed by nonlinear oscillator behavior exhibiting AC Josephson effect excitation.

Unmodulated intensity distribution ($I_{\mathrm{UM}}(\omega)$), frequency-modulated spectra ($I_{\mathrm{FM}}(\omega)$), and the spectral intensity ratio $\eta(	ext{fm}, 
u_c)$.
important_parameters:
Synchronization relaxation time ($	au_s$), modulation frequencies ($f_m$ up to $1	ext{ GHz}$), and central resonance frequencies ($
u_c \approx 840-870	ext{ GHz}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the spectral changes observed require introducing a finite relaxation time $	au_s$, which is interpreted as the lifetime of the macroscopic plasmon.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the double Gaussian peak structure in unmodulated spectra, and show how sideband intensities in FM spectra shift and change shape as a function of $f_m$ and assumed $	au_s$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from characterizing the static spectrum ($I_{\mathrm{UM}}(\omega)$) to analyzing the frequency-modulation response. It then introduces theoretical models incorporating finite relaxation times ($	au_s$) to quantitatively reproduce observed spectral transformations across varying $f_m$ regimes.
why_interesting: This work bridges solid-state superconductivity (high-Tc cuprates) with non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, using THz spectroscopy as a powerful probe for collective plasma oscillations and relaxation processes in strongly correlated materials.
